messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: production-streaming-eu p99 decode latency crossed 5s threshold (rule: streaming.decode.p99 > 4s). Alert at 2026-03-15T12:12:02Z. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/decode-latency
Chris: saw that. oncall? @Sanjay you good to take triage?
Sanjay: on it. paging in. quick summary: p95 ~220ms (normal ~80ms), p99 ~5.3s (normal ~500-700ms). Streaming stalls and client reconnects reported. Looks like tail-only, many requests succeed but a subset stall for entire stream.
Hana: FYI we rolled a kernel/compilepath upgrade yesterday to canary and then gradual rollout. It included TRT runtime bump (trt8.2.1 -> trt8.3.0) and a FlashAttention rebuild with new compiler flags (LTO + -march=native) — commit: 0b7d3f9a.
Jack: attaching logs from an affected host (streaming worker):
```
[2026-03-15T12:09:42Z] decode: start request id=mx-3a2
[2026-03-15T12:09:43Z] memory: pagefault handler evicting 128MB from kv_cache
[2026-03-15T12:09:45Z] decode: waiting for kv refill, stall 2100ms
[2026-03-15T12:11:46Z] decode: fatal stall > 120s, aborting stream
trace: kernel: mmap: excessive reclaim detected
```
Noting repeated "mmap excessive reclaim" lines.
Emily: running quick checks across fleet for kernel/build variants now. command: `ssh worker-1 'uname -r && cat /opt/runtime/version'` outputs:
```
worker-1: 5.19.16-redwood+
redwood-runtime 3.12.0 (trt 8.3.0, flashattn 1.4.0, compileflags: -O3 -flto -march=native)
worker-4: 5.19.16-redwood+
redwood-runtime 3.12.0 (trt 8.3.0, flashattn 1.4.0, compileflags: -O3 -flto -march=native)
canary-1: 5.19.12-redwood+
redwood-runtime 3.11.5 (trt 8.2.1, flashattn 1.3.2, compileflags: -O2)
```
Maya: support queue — two enterprise customers in EU reported stream timeouts, both hit around same timeframe. Customers seeing SDK reconnects and partial transcripts. Added to incident ticket INC-2026-132.
Sanjay: hypothesis: new TRT/FlashAttention build interacting with kernel allocator / mmap semantics under heavy KV cache churn causing pagefault-driven stalls. Could be LTO or -march changes enabling different memory access patterns. Also possible compilepath changed alignment that breaks our cache eviction heuristics.
Chris: options: 1) toggle runtime feature to disable FlashAttention (fast mitigation) 2) flip compile flag to non-LTO (hotpatch) 3) rollback worker kernel/runtime to previous version (safer but heavier). Which is lowest blast radius?
Jack: disabling FlashAttention at runtime is quick: set env RT_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1 for affected service and restart worker process. Patch is non-destructive and reversible. Rolling kernel requires node reboots and could affect capacity.
Sanjay: agree. plan: 1) apply RT_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1 to one canary AZ and observe 2) if metrics improve, rollout to remaining EU workers 3) start rollback plan for runtime build (rebuild without LTO) as follow-up.
deploy-bot: deploy started: env patch to production-streaming-eu/canary (RT_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1) by Sanjay at 2026-03-15T12:28:10Z. CI job: #build-7053.
Hana: running the env toggle now on canary set. command: `kubectl set env deploy/stream-worker RT_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1 -n prod-eu` and `kubectl rollout restart deploy/stream-worker`.
Jack: canary logs after toggle (first 6m):
```
[2026-03-15T12:30:15Z] decode: start request id=mx-8f1
[2026-03-15T12:30:15Z] memory: kv_cache hits stable
[2026-03-15T12:30:16Z] decode: token latency p99 420ms
```
Looks much better on canary.
deploy-bot: canary rollout SUCCESSFUL. 5/5 pods updated in prod-eu/canary.
Sanjay: metrics update: canary p99 back to ~480ms within 10m. Cluster-wide p99 still elevated for older nodes. Starting staged rollout to remaining EU pools. Rolling 1 AZ at a time.
Maya: customer comms: emailed impacted customers with temporary mitigation details and ETA for full rollout. Added note: we may request logs for any persistent failures.
Emily: I'm starting a fleet-wide query to identify nodes with trt8.3.0 + flashattn 1.4.0 and LTO enabled. Command: `rg "trt 8.3.0" -n /opt/runtime/* | sed -n '1,200p'` then we will schedule targeted env toggles.
Chris: please timebox full rollout to 45m and if any regression or failures appear, pause and escalate to rollback kernel version. Keep me updated every 15m.
Sanjay: acknowledged. rolling EU-eu-west-1 next (starting 12:44Z).
deploy-bot: starting staged rollout to prod-eu/eu-west-1 (batch size 10%).
Jack: note: while toggling FlashAttention helps, we should still prepare a rebuild without LTO and without -march=native; LTO may have changed codegen that worsens memory striding. Hana, can you spin a build?
Hana: on it. spawning build job #rebuild-7057 with flags: -O2 -fno-lto -march=x86-64. Estimate 35m build + canary smoke 15m.
Maya: updated INC-2026-132 with mitigation steps and timeline. Support is pinged to collect any residual logs.
Sanjay: once staged rollout completes and p99 normalizes for 30m, we'll declare mitigation. Otherwise, escalate to kernel/runtime rollback.
Chris: after handoff: Night oncall Noah will monitor from 18:00Z-06:00Z. leaving notes for Noah in the incident doc. Noah, please check: p95/p99, streaming reconnect errors, and any regression in throughput.
Noah: got it, I'll take night watch. ping me if anything regresses.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-132 (severity: Sev2) assigned to oncall team. Join channel #incident-INC-2026-132.
Maya: closing customer update loop for now. will post final note when we finish full rollout. :thumbsup:
Chris: thanks team. keep the thread updated and add any postmortem notes to the incident ticket.
